title: fix(skills): allow browsing with unrelated invalid configuration
body:
Closes #130569

## What Problem This Solves

An unrelated invalid configuration key prevents `skills`, `skills list`, `skills check`, and `skills info` from inspecting local skills, although the command catalog explicitly admits those browse routes with `configGuard: skip`.

## Changes and User Impact

Retains zhangguiping-xydt's shared-owner repair: use the existing non-observing best-effort config reader for browsing only, with plugin validation still skipped. Installation and other mutation callers continue using the strict reader. Explicit/cwd/default agent selection and Gateway error/fallback policy are unchanged. No new configuration, schema, SDK export, dependency or repair/migration behavior.

The earlier investigation by wangmiao0668000666 in closed, unmerged #112362 remains relevant context.

## Evidence

Built main `23ce62a0035a78be5050c5d9305ddb47168e6675` and contributor production head `4898d1ded743b3637c537f2ef582ee94032b9aec` in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. Subsequent changes only consolidate tests and document browse admission; production code remains the contributor's build.

Used the real built `dist/entry.js` CLI, an explicit task-owned profile and isolated HOME/config/state/workspace. The workspace contains a synthetic `proof-skill/SKILL.md`. Invalid configuration adds only `definitelyNotARealKey: true` to an otherwise valid configuration selecting that workspace. The implicit-local Gateway port is unavailable, so successful browsing traverses the shipped offline fallback, not a fixture inventory or mocked config reader.

Each command below ran **twice per ref** against invalid configuration:

| Command | Main, both runs | Candidate, both runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skills` | exit 1, unknown root key | exit 0, proof-skill displayed |
| `skills list --json` | exit 1, unknown root key | exit 0, proof-skill listed |
| `skills check --json` | exit 1, unknown root key | exit 0, proof-skill eligible |
| `skills info proof-skill --json` | exit 1, unknown root key | exit 0, fixture metadata returned |
| `skills install <synthetic-local-source>` | exit 1, invalid configuration | exit 1, invalid configuration |
| `config get gateway.port` | exit 1, invalid configuration | exit 1, invalid configuration |

Mutation control uses a real local skill source, so it needs no external registry. Strict configuration admission rejects it before installation; the destination is never created. The strict error explicitly names the invalid root key rather than an unrelated argument or download failure.

**Valid-config control:** all four browse commands also ran twice per ref with valid configuration, exited 0 and returned the same synthetic skill. Total matrix: **40 real commands**. Configuration bytes and the source SKILL.md hash were checked unchanged after every repetition. No real credentials, live Gateway, external skill registry, model call or channel delivery is claimed.

## Focused Checks and Simplification

- Four focused files passed: **62 tests**, 8.02 s Vitest duration (skills commands, verify, Workshop, and command startup policy). The final compact command suite also passed (34 tests, 2.01 s), and changed TypeScript formatting passed.
- The existing default/check JSON cases now make the strict async reader reject while requiring the selected-workspace browse result. Both fail on main with CLI exit 1 and pass on candidate. Existing workspace/agent selection and explicit-remote/no-fallback assertions remain; the remote browse fixture now configures the browse reader explicitly.
- Consolidated the separate added browse table into existing Commander-routing cases and simplified duplicate unused-call setup. The shipped-CLI matrix above independently exercises all four browse routes and strict install refusal. Removed the no-longer-needed growth allocation; no new mock factory or production seam.
- Whole-PR delta: production **net 0** (6 added / 6 removed), tests **net 0**, docs **+5**. Broad checks belong to exact-head PR CI.

The contributor's prior latest-stable upgrade/preservation capture is retained below and is **contributor-supplied evidence, not a maintainer rerun**. This repair changes no stored format or upgrade owner.

<details>
<summary>Latest-stable upgrade and preservation capture</summary>

Latest stable release at verification: `v2026.10.9` (published 2026-10-29). Independently installed the official locked npm package in an isolated prefix, then created a fresh workspace with the same local skill and an `operator-notes.txt` sentinel. The valid stable config selected that workspace, local Gateway mode, disabled memory plugin, and a synthetic local-only auth token. All commands below use the same state/config across the binary switch. No managed Gateway/service or real account was involved.

Actual stable CLI stdout (`node <stable-prefix>/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs ...`):

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55)
exit=0
$ openclaw config set messages.responsePrefix upgrade-preserved
Updated messages.responsePrefix. No gateway restart needed.
exit=0
$ openclaw config get messages.responsePrefix
upgrade-preserved
exit=0
```

Stable `skills info proof-skill --json` also exited 0. Switched the executable to the fixed source build (`node openclaw.mjs`) against the existing stable-created state and ran `doctor --fix --non-interactive` (exit 0), following Doctor's migration guidance. A diagnostic-only first attempt (`doctor --non-interactive`) correctly refused the stable database schema migration without backed-up custody; the fix-mode run on a fresh equivalent stable fixture completed the supported migration. Doctor writes normalized config/defaults, so config bytes are not expected to be identical across migration; existing setting values are checked explicitly. After migration, actual stdout:

```text
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.workspace
/tmp/oc-130569-proof/upgrade-state-verified/workspace
exit=0
$ openclaw config get messages.responsePrefix
upgrade-preserved
exit=0
```

Then introduced only `definitelyNotARealKey: true` into that upgraded config. All four browse commands exited 0 and included `proof-skill`; strict `config get gateway.port` exited 1. Actual complete `skills info proof-skill --json` stdout from the upgraded invalid-config fixture:

```json
{
  "name": "proof-skill",
  "description": "Stable upgrade preservation fixture.",
  "source": "openclaw-workspace",
  "bundled": false,
  "filePath": "/tmp/oc-130569-proof/upgrade-state-verified/workspace/skills/proof-skill/SKILL.md",
  "baseDir": "/tmp/oc-130569-proof/upgrade-state-verified/workspace/skills/proof-skill",
  "skillKey": "proof-skill",
  "always": false,
  "disabled": false,
  "blockedByAllowlist": false,
  "eligible": true,
  "missing": {
    "bins": [],
    "anyBins": [],
    "env": [],
    "config": [],
    "os": []
  },
  "configChecks": [],
  "blockedByAgentFilter": false,
  "platformIncompatible": false,
  "modelVisible": true,
  "userInvocable": true,
  "commandVisible": true,
  "requirements": {
    "bins": [],
    "anyBins": [],
    "env": [],
    "config": [],
    "os": []
  },
  "install": []
}
```

Actual preservation assertions printed by the harness (SHA-256 values compare original stable-created file bytes with the migrated/fixed run):

```text
PRESERVATION {"selectedWorkspace": "/tmp/oc-130569-proof/upgrade-state-verified/workspace", "setting": "upgrade-preserved", "skillSha256": "486760c02851a16fbc585d095345246d8813d7af07a9233b570ecd35212d7d2e", "workspaceFileSha256": "a0d5d2070ad5b2d8c8c9dd416f782247f2d1727ef6de0593e37edcb7557bfc85", "skillAndWorkspaceBytesUnchanged": true, "configBytesUnchanged": false}
POST_UPGRADE_INVALID_CONFIG browse=4/4 strict=reject config/skill/workspace-bytes=unchanged
```

The second line additionally checks that browse/strict inspection did not change the now-invalid config bytes. This covers the CLI config/workspace/skill boundary; a running Gateway, live channel/model, and managed update installation lifecycle were not exercised.

</details>

## Compatibility and Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores strict browse loading; no persistent schema/config migration. Blast radius is read-only skills inspection when configuration is invalid. Mutations remain strict, existing agent selection remains authoritative, and explicit/remote Gateway failures retain the existing fallback restrictions. Browsing does not silently repair or rewrite invalid configuration.
